newsitem.title: DUBAI: Over 100 Indians die in Saudi haj blaze-ambassador.
newsitem.headline: Over 100 Indians die in Saudi haj blaze-ambassador.

text.p: More than 100 Indian haj pilgrims are believed to be among the at least 181 Moslems killed when a fire raged through 70,000 tents at a temporary haj compound near the holy city of Mecca in Saudi Arabia, India's ambassador said.
"Our assessment is that the number of Indian dead runs into three figures," Ambassador Mohammad Hamad Ansari told Reuters by telephone from Mecca.
"It's a distressing situation," the ambassador said. Some 80,000 Indians are performing this year's haj, he added.

"Now we are trying to identify bodies and inform the next of kin, which is not very easy because all the pilgrims are on the move. Even getting a head count of those missing is difficult," he said. Pilgrims were heading to Mena from Mecca, 11 km (seven miles) away, on Tuesday on the first stage of the haj.

Ansari said he had visited the tent city, parts of which had been razed to the ground. "It's a traumatic experience for everyone who witnessed the fire, but there is a great deal of devotion among the pilgrims who continue to perform their prayers and haj rituals," he said.
Saudi state radio said at least 181 people were killed and 800 were injured by the blaze.
